title: Time management section by section
lines: On the shorter GRE, every section is tight. Most people who run out of time do not work too slowly in general; they spend four minutes on one stubborn question and then rush the last five. Good pacing means deciding in advance how long each kind of question deserves and leaving the hard ones for later.
## The numbers
> Verbal: 18 min for 12 questions, then 23 min for 15 questions (about 90 seconds each)
> Quant: 21 min for 12 questions, then 26 min for 15 questions (about 105 seconds each)
> Essay: 30 min for one Issue task
## Target time per question type
Aim for the lower end of each range on most questions. That builds a buffer for review and for the odd hard question.
- Sentence Equivalence: 45-60 seconds.
- Text Completion, one blank: 45-60 seconds.
- Text Completion, two blanks: 75-90 seconds.
- Text Completion, three blanks: 90-120 seconds.
- Reading, short passage (one paragraph): about 2 minutes to read, then 45-75 seconds per question.
- Reading, long passage: about 3 minutes to read, then 60-75 seconds per question.
- Argument paragraph: about 90 seconds for the paragraph and its one question.
- Quantitative Comparison: 60-75 seconds.
- Quant multiple choice and numeric entry: 90-120 seconds.
- Data Interpretation: about 2 minutes per question, including a first look at the chart.
! Vocabulary questions (TC and SE) are your time bank in Verbal. Answer them briskly so that reading passages get the time they need.
## The two-pass method
Inside a section you can move freely, so use two passes.
- Pass 1: Go through every question in order. If you can answer it within its target time, answer it. If it looks long or you get stuck, choose your best guess, mark it and move on.
- Pass 2: Use the review screen to go back to marked questions, starting with the ones you felt closest to solving.
This method guarantees that you see every question, including easy ones near the end. It also means every question already has an answer, so running out of time costs you nothing extra.
## Mark and move: the 2-minute rule

Set a personal limit. In Verbal, if a question passes 2 minutes and you are not close, mark it. In Quant, use 2.5 minutes. The longer you stay on a question that is not working, the less likely you are to solve it, and the more you take from easier points later.

> Example: In Quant section 1 you reach question 6, a probability problem. After 90 seconds you have two possible methods and no answer. Pick the choice that seems most likely, mark it, and go to question 7. You return with 4 minutes left and solve it calmly.
## Checkpoints
Instead of looking at the timer after every question, check at fixed points.
- Verbal section 1 (12 questions, 18 min): about 12 minutes left after question 4, 6 minutes left after question 8.
- Verbal section 2 (15 questions, 23 min): about 15 minutes left after question 5, 8 minutes left after question 10.
- Quant section 1 (12 questions, 21 min): about 14 minutes left after question 4, 7 minutes left after question 8.
- Quant section 2 (15 questions, 26 min): about 17 minutes left after question 5, 9 minutes left after question 10.
If you are behind at a checkpoint, mark the next long question you meet instead of starting it.
## Section 1 versus section 2

Because section 1 decides the difficulty of section 2, accuracy in section 1 is worth slightly more than speed. Spend your buffer there on checking. In section 2, keep moving: the questions may be harder, and finishing matters.
## Reading passages
- Read the passage once, actively, noting the main point and the role of each paragraph in a few words.
- Do not try to memorize details. Go back to the passage for each detail question.
- If a passage is on a topic you find heavy, answer its general question first (the main idea), then decide whether the other questions are worth the time.
## Essay timing
- 3-5 minutes: read the task, choose a position and plan two or three reasons with examples.
- 20-22 minutes: write the introduction, body paragraphs and a short conclusion.
- 3-5 minutes: reread and fix errors.
## Training your pace in this app
- Do practice sets with the timer, and compare your time per question with the targets above.
- In mock tests, note any question that took more than 3 minutes. That topic needs work, or you need to practice letting go.
- After each mock, check how many questions you left for the last minute. If it was more than two, use the checkpoints next time.
